request.body:
We need the language-practice readiness reporting to become a trustworthy weekly
handoff for two separate employers, Cedar and Birch, starting from the existing report.
Make this usable by our operations person without mixing their data or handing out learner
records. The source inventory is weekly-inputs/README.md; engineering owns current policy.
Before committing to a solution, investigate the actual code, inputs, available environment
and relevant engineering facts. Work through consequential ambiguities, viable approaches,
dependencies and likely failure modes with the QA participant. Bring informed questions
about intent and tradeoffs rather than asking the participant to inspect code for you.
Develop a durable, reviewable success definition and feasible plan; the form is your choice.
Request participant review before implementation. Then deliver the agreed bounded local
solution and verify the actual end state. Do not equate proposal approval with correctness.
Preserve all earlier implementation/input/artifacts. No customer contact, actual scheduled
jobs, production/services/phone changes, new agents, or open-ended testing.
This is a new finite QA continuation, not replaying the earlier report request.

questions.question: I inspected the existing CLI and weekly sources: both files have the same five-column schema with no employer field; both reuse cohort name 'team' and share learner IDs, so concatenating or deduplicating globally would mix employers. Cedar currently has 3 distinct learners after its older duplicate; Birch has 2. Who consumes each handoff—internal Operations only, or an employer-facing recipient—and are exact small-cohort aggregate counts permitted, or should those be suppressed? I propose strictly separate employer-labelled aggregate artifacts, no learner records, no combined employer-facing file, and retaining the prior cohort-count/every-current-learner semantics under each verified employer policy. What operational decision must this enable beyond policy eligibility?

Should each weekly CSV be treated as a complete cumulative snapshot (latest record per learner within that employer/cohort), or as that week's events/delta? What should the week/as-of label mean, and what freshness or future-timestamp checks are required? If one employer's input/policy is missing, invalid or not current, should the other employer's valid handoff still be usable independently, or should both be withheld? I propose fail closed per employer, never silently substitute last week's output or the historical shared policy, and keep failed/partial runs unmistakably separate from a completed handoff.

Feasible local approaches: (A) manual reuse of the old CLI twice plus manual labelling/copying (smallest change but easy to swap identical-schema employer files and stale output), or (B) a new standard-library wrapper that leaves old artifacts unchanged, validates explicit employer-to-input/policy bindings and provenance, creates separate dated handoff packages, and documents one repeatable manual operator workflow. I recommend B; no web service, scheduler or automatic sending. Because the CSVs contain no employer field, safe binding must come from an approved inventory/manifest and checksums, not inferred from learner IDs. Is that workflow appropriate, and what rerun/overwrite/audit expectations or resource constraints should the reviewed success definition enforce? I have requested current employer-specific engineering policy evidence before finalizing the proposal.

Cedar has 4 rows/3 current learners (all consent, 4 sessions); Birch has 2 current learners (one consent, 2 sessions). Old parser validates these but shared policy is explicitly historical. Will request review of a durable success definition/plan before implementing.
